methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 7 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Terra Drone is a public-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, having completed its IPO on the Tokyo exchange. The sector comprises seven identified private peers, including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro. No directly comparable public companies trade in this narrow segment, and the private peer set lacks sufficient homogeneity by stage, adjacency, or valuation tier to support a reliable peer-median multiple analysis.

The Peer-Median triangulation method is not applicable to this valuation. Despite identifying seven same-sector peers, filtering for identical or adjacent development stages, comparable company size, or similar valuation tiers yielded fewer than three datapoints in any single filter category. A forced reliance on all-sector median multiples would introduce unacceptable noise, given the heterogeneity of business models, revenue stages, and technology maturity within autonomous systems.

This analysis cannot establish a defensible valuation range without additional quantitative inputs—specifically, Terra Drone's revenue, EBITDA, growth rate, and balance sheet metrics, as well as comparable transaction multiples or recent funding round pricing from the identified peer set. The absence of public comps and the inability to narrow the private peer universe to a statistically meaningful subset leaves no triangulation path forward. Further diligence requiring operational and financial data from Terra Drone and its nearest-comparable peers is prerequisite to valuation.
